newsitem.title: UK: OPEC June crude output dn 580k bpd to 26.4 mln-IEA.
newsitem.headline: OPEC June crude output dn 580k bpd to 26.4 mln-IEA.

text.p: Crude oil production by the 11 members of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) fell by 580,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.39 million bpd in June, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday.

The fall was largely the result of the lack of Iraqi exports, suspended since late May when the first $2 billion cash limit set by the United Nations oil-for-food deal was reached, which more than exceeded production increases elsewhere.
"Iraqi production fell to its pre-December level of 550,000 bpd, a drop of 770,000 bpd from the previous month," the Paris-based agency said in its monthly Oil Market Report.
"This was only partly offset by gains in production from the UAE and Nigeria," it said.
UAE output rebounded after field maintenance in May while Nigeria enjoyed a relatively "uneventful month".

"Production in the Bonny and Forcados areas is estimated to have increased by 40,000 bpd, in the absence of any major civil disturbances, and Odudu output is assumed to have contributed an incremental 20,000 bpd, after completing maintenance activities," the IEA said.
Saudi Arabian and Kuwaiti production was stable but there were also small increases in Venezuela, Libya and Iran.
Output fell slightly in Algeria, Indonesia and Qatar.
The IEA includes in its calculation of Saudi output almost 150,000 bpd of production in Saudi territory gifted to Bahrain.
